transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time. It's probably just normal stress or getting older, you know? But... I guess I've been having a little trouble keeping my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it lately. Even when it's really important. 

Like, at work—I do computer support—I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and... well, ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the exact same log entries three times, and I still don't know what they say. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. 

Does that... does that sound like the kind of thing I should be coming in for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and giving you what you need.
Did you have similar trouble paying attention or finishing tasks when you were a child?

Oh, um... well, as a kid... I mean, I wasn't a troublemaker or anything. I hope it doesn't sound like I was. But, uh, my mother actually still jokes about my old report cards from grade school. She always makes sure to point out that the teachers said I was a really bright boy. Just... maybe a little too enthusiastic? 

I guess I had a bit of a habit of blurting out answers in class before I was called on. And, um, staying in my seat was apparently pretty difficult for me. I just had a lot of energy, I think. And the homework... I'd actually do the assignments, I really tried to, but somehow I'd always manage to lose them before I could turn them in. 

It's a little embarrassing to look back on, but I suppose kids are just disorganized sometimes, right? Is that... is that the kind of background information you need? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.
Did these concentration problems start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Well, um... I guess it really got bad about, oh, a year and ten months ago? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses, but... well, I was let go from my old job around then. 

I mean, it wasn't a bad firing or anything, just a restructuring, you know how companies are. But at that job, I had all these routines and systems set up that kind of... held everything together for me? And once those were gone, it just felt like everything sort of unraveled. 

I've really been trying my best to get a handle on it since then, but it's just been causing so much trouble lately. I feel terrible even complaining about it, because I know people go through much worse. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overcomplicating things for you.
